mechanism: Soybean meal crack spread slope captures crush margin expansion momentum where profit growth leads price direction. When soybean crush margins trend higher, processors increase output, initially tightening meal supply before volume responds. The slope direction of crack spreads predicts meal price continuation: expanding margins signal strong meal demand relative to bean availability, creating forward price pressure via inventory drawdowns.
symbol_fit: M is central to the crush chain - meal price reflects protein demand from livestock feed against bean supply. Unlike soybeans or oil, meal has concentrated industrial offtake (feed mills) making crack spread slope a leading indicator. Crush margin momentum predicts meal price direction before spot price discovery.
